title: Adjuvant gemcitabine + cisplatin
indication_text: Adjuvant treatment of muscle-invasive and/or node-positive, non-metastatic predominantly transitional-cell upper-tract urothelial carcinoma after surgery.
purpose: Reduce the risk of upper-tract urothelial cancer returning after surgery.
schedule_label: Days 1 and 8 · every 21 days · four cycles
schedule_summary: Gemcitabine is given on days 1 and 8 and cisplatin on day 1. The 21-day cycle is planned four times after surgery for eligible upper-tract urothelial cancer. Treatment may be delayed or adjusted for safety.
administration_text: Gemcitabine runs into a vein over 30 minutes; cisplatin over 60 minutes with prescribed fluids. Review, preparation, blood tests and anti-sickness medicines add to the visit time.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests on day 1; blood count and creatinine before day 8. Symptoms, hearing, nerves and hydration are reviewed before treatment.
safety_note: Follow your own prescription and hospital instructions. This information supports a discussion; it does not authorise treatment.
urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, shaking chills, suddenly feeling unwell, unusual bleeding, new breathlessness, very little urine, severe rash or vomiting that prevents drinking. Follow your hospital’s temperature and contact instructions. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or seizures: call 112/999.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, fatigue, flu-like symptoms and swelling
Rash, sore mouth and liver-test changes
Uncommon or rare serious lung inflammation, kidney injury including haemolytic uraemic syndrome, severe skin reactions and capillary leak

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Kidney injury and low magnesium or other electrolyte changes
Hearing loss or ringing in the ears, which may be lasting
Numbness or tingling from nerve damage, sometimes lasting
Low blood counts, serious infection and bleeding

evidence.title: POUT · final report 2024
evidence.summary: POUT randomised 261 people after surgery for high-risk upper-tract urothelial cancer to four cycles of gemcitabine/platinum or surveillance. At five years, disease-free survival was 62% versus 45% (hazard ratio 0.55, 95% confidence interval 0.38–0.80).
evidence.intro: POUT randomised 261 people after surgery for high-risk upper-tract urothelial cancer to four cycles of gemcitabine/platinum or surveillance. At five years, disease-free survival was 62% versus 45% (hazard ratio 0.55, 95% confidence interval 0.38–0.80).
evidence.caveat: Disease-free survival means being alive without a recorded recurrence; it is not the same as overall survival. The trial included cisplatin or carboplatin according to kidney function, so the whole-trial result is not a cisplatin-only estimate or permission for automatic substitution.
evidence.interpretation: Disease-free survival means being alive without a recorded recurrence; it is not the same as overall survival. questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Reduce the risk of upper-tract urothelial cancer returning after surgery. This treatment follows surgery of the upper urinary tract. It aims to treat microscopic disease that scans cannot show. Ongoing urology and oncology surveillance remains necessary; your team sets the imaging and bladder-surveillance schedule.

Gemcitabine is given on days 1 and 8 and cisplatin on day 1. The 21-day cycle is planned four times after surgery for eligible upper-tract urothelial cancer. Treatment may be delayed or adjusted for safety.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
